title: Trinity
definition: The Trinity means there is one true God who eternally exists as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, three distinct persons sharing one divine being.
summary: The Trinity means there is one true God who eternally exists as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, three distinct persons sharing one divine being.
christFocus: Jesus reveals the triune life of God: sent by the Father, conceived by the Spirit, anointed for ministry, crucified for sinners, raised in power, and worshiped as Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Trinity is not a puzzle invented by theologians; it is the way Scripture reveals the one true God. The Father is God, the Son is God, and the Holy Spirit is God, yet God is one.

This doctrine protects the Gospel. The Father sends, the Son saves, and the Spirit gives life. Salvation is not the work of a distant deity but the gracious work of the triune God drawing sinners into fellowship with Himself.

The Trinity also shows that God has never been lonely, needy, or loveless. From eternity, Father, Son, and Spirit are perfect in glory, love, and fellowship. Believers are invited into communion with this God through Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers find the Trinity intimidating, but this doctrine is not meant to confuse them; it is meant to lead them to worship. The God who saves is greater than human imagination and nearer than sinners deserve.

It also keeps believers from reducing Jesus or the Spirit to less than Scripture reveals. Christian faith, prayer, worship, and discipleship depend on the triune God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Worship the Father, trust the Son, and depend on the Holy Spirit. Let the Trinity deepen your prayer, your wonder, and your confidence that salvation rests in God's own faithful work from beginning to end.
